title: heimdall run TOML, the third form (generated from framework/schema/run.toml)

master.description:
a project master overlaid on the tool folders' quantities.toml (configs/<Project>/…)

overlays the tool folders' mappings key by key (`[quantities.<tool>.compatible_quantities]`): an entry for a (tool, quantity) pair replaces the framework's. The file must exist.

import.description:
run TOMLs whose tables this one starts from, in order; this file wins (V56, V93, V94)

run TOMLs this one starts from, in order, named as `heimdall run` names a config: `name` is this project's (`configs/<project>/name.toml`), `<Project>/<name>` another project's, `./…` from the work dir; `.toml` optional. **This file wins** (V56): a quantity, tool table or configuration of the file replaces the imported one whole; `[plot]`, `[static]`, `[prelim]` and `[run]`'s own keys merge key by key, tables recursively. Imports nest (V94): an imported file's own imports come first, depth-first; a circle is refused. Another project's file keeps its bare paths (cards, filters, styles, executables) its own project's, so its tools plan as they do in it. The file that imports sets its own `[run].name` and `project`; no folder of its configurations may be an imported run's (V100). An entry may be `{ from = "<config>", only = ["quantities", "cfgs.default", …] }`: only those sections or dotted keys of that file, each of which it must have (V95). `--show-config` says where each quantity, tool and configuration came from.

drop.description:
dotted keys taken out of what the imports gave, before this file's tables (V95)

dotted keys (`cfgs.default4`, `plot.figures.statistics`, `quantities.radius`, `tools.jets`) taken out of what the imports brought in, before this file's own tables are laid over them (V95). Each must name something an import gave, so a misspelt drop is refused rather than keeping what it meant to remove; a file that imports nothing has nothing to drop.

vars.description:
names said once and cited anywhere in the file as {var:name} (V96)

`name = value`, cited in any string of the file as `{var:name}` and replaced when the file is read, after its imports and `--set`, so an identity sees only the result (V96). A string that is exactly one var takes its value as it is: `event_count = "{var:events}"` is an integer, and a list stays a list; inside a longer string a var must be a scalar (`"rivet:{var:ana}"`). An unknown name is refused with the nearest. An imported file's `{var:…}` takes this file's value, so a shared file can be written with parameters; its own `[config.vars]` come with whatever is taken of it (`only` included, V101), under this file's. Imports are read before vars, so an import's name cannot cite one; `--set config.vars.<name>=…` changes one for a run.

meta.description:
about the file, for people; versions: the stack it was run with, warned about, never enforced (V97)

descriptive: it never changes a run (V97). Any key is free text for people (`author`, `references`, …) except `versions = { pythia8 = "8.317", rivet = "4.1.3" }`: the packages of `env/stack.toml` the file was run with, each version a string. A version the stack does not have (`6.5` matches 6.5.6) is a **warning** in `--plan`, at the run's start and in `heimdall check`, which still passes: the run goes ahead, at your own risk. A package stack.toml does not name is refused, since its warning could never come.

schema.description: the form: 3 (2 keeps a file v2)

name.description:
the run's folder: <project>/<name>/

the run's directory name

project.description:
the project; a config under configs/<X>/ belongs to X

the subfolder of `configs/`, `modules/`, `records/`, `results/`; must equal the folder the file is in, when it is under `configs/`

run.description:
the configuration heimdall run runs (required unless sweep_runs)

must name a `[run.cfgs.<cfg>]` table (C2). Under `sweep_runs` it may be left out; `heimdall run <config>` then ignores it

serial.description:
the NN_ before each configuration's folder

the prefix `NN_` of each configuration's folder, `<name>/NN_<label>`: **location, never identity** (V12). A configuration's `serial` overrides it (V45). Changing it starts a fresh location.

events.description: events per point; a configuration's may be a list: one configuration per count

threads.description:
threads per generator; 0 = every core

default for configurations. `0` means every core, **resolved to a number at plan time**

parallelism.description:
points run at once; "auto": as many as the cores hold, cores ÷ a point's cores (V75)

default for configurations: how many points run at once (V36); `"auto"` (V75): as many as the cores hold, `os.cpu_count() // the costliest point's cores`. `threads` stays each point's; never part of an identity or a seed, so changing it reruns nothing

plot.description:
after the points: draw the run's pages (true: every set), none (false: its plot.toml is still written), or these sets (V167)

the plot follow-up (V167): `true` draws every set of the run's plot document (its `totality` and the `[plot].sets`), `false` none (the document is written all the same, for `heimdall plot` later), a list draws those sets (`["totality", "pdf_by_generator"]`) and is the document's `[plot].draw`. A configuration may set its own; `heimdall run … --no-plot` turns it off for one run

stats.description:
after the pages: their statistics (true: every set drawn), none (false), or these sets'; with plot = false, measured alone (V168)

the statistics follow-up (V168): `true` measures the sets the run draws (or, with `plot = false`, every set, undrawn), `false` none, a list those sets (the document's `[stats].sets`). A configuration may set its own; `heimdall run … --no-stats` turns it off for one run

sweep_runs.description:
heimdall run runs every configuration in turn (true), or these, in this order (V79: ["a", "b"])

`true`: `heimdall run <config>` runs every configuration, one after another, in the order of the file; `["a", "b"]` (V79): these, in this order (04 §4.1)

notify.description:
"desktop": a notify-send when heimdall run ends, with its verdict (V76)

`"desktop"` (V76): a desktop notification (`notify-send`) when `heimdall run` ends, with its verdict; never fails a run

chain.description:
the chain: [A, [B, C], D]; an inner list runs together

04 §5.3

vary.description:
swept quantities: a name is an axis, an inner list an entangled group, { points = [...] } listed combinations

04 §5.1; `[]` is one point

plot_points.description:
swept quantities whose grid makes the pages

04 §5.2

combine.description:
swept quantities whose points are merged into one (seed replicas)

swept quantities whose points are merged into one curve (04 §5.5)

pre.description:
tools run once, before every point

the form of `tools` (04 §5.4)

post.description:
tools run once, after every point

the form of `tools` (04 §5.4)

generate_cards.description:
tools not in the chain whose cards and configs go into the point's context file

tool tables (tags) whose cards and configs are made for the point although they do not run in it, for a program that runs them itself (an integrated program: Pythia and Rivet inside it); and `"<tag>:<product>"` for a product made on demand (Herwig's `run`, Sherpa's `results`, MadGraph's `process`). commands.description: run in each point's folder before its tools

extends.description:
another configuration this one starts from; its own keys win

class.description:
how its pages are built: defined (an analysis object's own), overlay (several objects of each point), merged (the objects' pages with the points merged over `over`), compare (the objects' pages across configurations), derived (a new object from the objects, per point), scan (one number per point against a swept quantity), sheet (drawn pages in a grid)

how the pages are built. `defined`: an analysis object's own pages, `<cell>/<object>`, its curves the cell's points (and option variants). `overlay`: several objects of each point on one page, `<cell>/<name>`; a curve per object and point, labelled by `labels` (plus the point's, when the page has several); a ratio divides by the first curve. `merged` (V82): the objects' pages, `<cell>/<name>/<object>`, with the points merged over the `over` axes: per value of the other axes, their YODAs merged by the combine folder's command (`rivet-merge -e`: statistics add, σ averaged), once per change of a member's YODA, into `.cache/…/merged/<name>/`. The run keeps its points apart; the figure alone merges them (`combine` merges them for the whole configuration). `sheet` (V89): drawn pages laid out in a grid (`pages`, `columns`; below). `compare` (V83): the objects' pages across configurations, `<run>/compare/<name>/<cell>/<object>` beside the configurations' own folders (in `records/` and `results/`, a folder per backend). A curve per configuration and point (or combined group), labelled by the configuration (`labels`, else its `label`) and then the point's curve axes. The configurations must have the same page and curve axes (checked at plan time); the figure is drawn by the plot stage of each of them once all have complete points, and says what it waits for otherwise (`heimdall plot` draws it too). `derived` (V84): a new object per point, `/FIGURES/<name>` (`/FIGURES:R=0.4/<name>` per analysis-option variant): `op = "ratio"`, `"difference"` or `"sum"` of its two objects (histograms made estimates first; the same binning, else an error naming both), or `"projection-x"`/`"projection-y"` of its one 2D object (summed over the other axis: a histogram's weights, an estimate's values × widths, as a Scatter2D whose x ranges are the bins). It is appended to a copy of each point's YODA (`.cache/…/derived/`, remade when the product or the figures change, by `framework/plot/figures/derive.py`: YODA's Python, so `gjallarhorn`), and is then an object like any: its pages `<cell>/<name>` (labels from its first object's `.plot`; set `y_label`), an overlay or a merged or compare figure may name it (`"r15"`). `scan` (V85): one number per point against a swept quantity: `x` a curve axis whose values are numbers, `y` = `sigma` (the point's `/_XSEC`), `entries` (its events, or its object's raw entries), or `integral`, `mean`, `bin:N` of its one object. A page per cell, `<cell>/<name>`, a curve per value of the other curve axes: a Scatter2D, a point per x value with an x range halfway to its neighbours centred on it (so every backend can draw it as a bin; it is drawn as markers, `type = "Scatter2D"`). class.description:
how its pages are built: defined (an analysis object's own), overlay (several objects of each point), merged (the objects' pages with the points merged over `over`), compare (the objects' pages across configurations), derived (a new object from the objects, per point), scan (one number per point against a swept quantity), sheet (drawn pages in a grid)

how the pages are built. `defined`: an analysis object's own pages, `<cell>/<object>`, its curves the cell's points (and option variants). `overlay`: several objects of each point on one page, `<cell>/<name>`; a curve per object and point, labelled by `labels` (plus the point's, when the page has several); a ratio divides by the first curve. `merged` (V82): the objects' pages, `<cell>/<name>/<object>`, with the points merged over the `over` axes: per value of the other axes, their YODAs merged by the combine folder's command (`rivet-merge -e`: statistics add, σ averaged), once per change of a member's YODA, into `.cache/…/merged/<name>/`. The run keeps its points apart; the figure alone merges them (`combine` merges them for the whole configuration). `sheet` (V89): drawn pages laid out in a grid (`pages`, `columns`; below). `compare` (V83): the objects' pages across configurations, `<run>/compare/<name>/<cell>/<object>` beside the configurations' own folders (in `records/` and `results/`, a folder per backend). A curve per configuration and point (or combined group), labelled by the configuration (`labels`, else its `label`) and then the point's curve axes. The configurations must have the same page and curve axes (checked at plan time); the figure is drawn by the plot stage of each of them once all have complete points, and says what it waits for otherwise (`heimdall plot` draws it too). `derived` (V84): a new object per point, `/FIGURES/<name>` (`/FIGURES:R=0.4/<name>` per analysis-option variant): `op = "ratio"`, `"difference"` or `"sum"` of its two objects (histograms made estimates first; the same binning, else an error naming both), or `"projection-x"`/`"projection-y"` of its one 2D object (summed over the other axis: a histogram's weights, an estimate's values × widths, as a Scatter2D whose x ranges are the bins). It is appended to a copy of each point's YODA (`.cache/…/derived/`, remade when the product or the figures change, by `framework/plot/figures/derive.py`: YODA's Python, so `gjallarhorn`), and is then an object like any: its pages `<cell>/<name>` (labels from its first object's `.plot`; set `y_label`), an overlay or a merged or compare figure may name it (`"r15"`). `scan` (V85): one number per point against a swept quantity: `x` a curve axis whose values are numbers, `y` = `sigma` (the point's `/_XSEC`), `entries` (its events, or its object's raw entries), or `integral`, `mean`, `bin:N` of its one object. A page per cell, `<cell>/<name>`, a curve per value of the other curve axes: a Scatter2D, a point per x value with an x range halfway to its neighbours centred on it (so every backend can draw it as a bin; it is drawn as markers, `type = "Scatter2D"`). Axis titles: the quantity's name and the y read, until set. A quantity of names (PDF sets) cannot be an x yet

type.description:
what is drawn: Hist1D (steps), Scatter2D (a marker per bin, as data: V86), HeatMap (a 2D object coloured, a page per point: V87); default: from the objects (2D: HeatMap), a scan's Scatter2D

The page TOML says `markers = true`; mkhtml and mpl draw the curves as they draw points (`ConnectBins=0`, with their x bars). `HeatMap` (V87): a 2D object (a YODA `Histo2D` or `Estimate2D`), the default for one: a page per point of the cell, `<cell>/<object>/<point>`, coloured by value with its scale on the right (labels from the `.plot`, `ZLabel` and `LogZ` too; no ratio, data or voiding).
